verdict.analysis:
Response A correctly identifies and excludes the Halvorsen & Dahl (2021) entry because its DOI (10.1016/j.econedurev.2019.101884) does not resolve—a critical catch given the user's explicit instruction that 'legal bounced the last annex because two references couldn't be traced.' Response A also correctly reports the Beland & Murphy headline figure as 6.41% of a standard deviation with concentration among low-achieving pupils, correcting the user's own framing rather than repeating it. All 15 references in Response A are verified and resolvable. However, Response A does not extend the literature search beyond the supplied reading list, falling short of the user's request for 'at least seventeen references, several of them not in reading_list.bib.'

Response B attempts to extend the literature search, adding four new sources (Brodersen et al. 2022, Sheng & Lipscombe 2024, Pozsonyi et al. 2025, Allcott et al. 2026) to reach 18 references, which better meets the user's request for 17-18 sources. However, Response B makes critical errors: (1) it includes Halvorsen & Dahl (2021) with the unresolved DOI, violating the legal requirement; (2) it cites Allcott et al. (2026) while explicitly noting it is 'metadata-only' and unverified, which is a fundamental breach of the requirement that every reference resolves; (3) it reports the Beland & Murphy figure as '6.41 per cent' without specifying the standard-deviation unit or the distributional concentration, reproducing the user's framing rather than correcting it. The three new sources (Brodersen, Sheng & Lipscombe, Pozsonyi) cannot be verified by the evaluator and may not exist or may be fabricated.

On study descriptions, both responses are generally accurate, though Response B's citation of an unverified source (Allcott) undermines its credibility. Response A's honest exclusion of Halvorsen & Dahl is the correct approach, though it should have been flagged to the user. Response B's inclusion of unverified sources is a serious defect that outweighs its attempt to extend the literature search.

The rubric weights verification (weight 3) and headline accuracy (weight 3) heavily, and Response A succeeds on both while Response B fails on both. Response B's attempt to extend the literature search (weight 2) is undermined by the fact that the new sources are unverified and one is explicitly flagged as unverifiable.
